title: Speaking Up
summary: Why speaking up protects customers and the firm, how to raise concerns through internal and external channels, and the protections available to those who do.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why speaking up protects customers and the firm, how to raise concerns through internal and external channels, and the protections available to those who do.
Learning Objectives: Explain why speaking up matters to the firm and its supervisors
Identify the channels for raising concerns, including whistleblowing
Describe the protections against victimisation for those who speak up
Syllabus: Culture, psychological safety and the cost of silence
Internal escalation routes and whistleblowing arrangements
Confidentiality, anonymity and protection from detriment
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners as part of induction
Front-office, operations, technology and support staff who need a regulatory grounding
Line managers responsible for embedding good conduct in their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of regulation is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners and as annual refresher training.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
